sources.title: MIVUBI Client Feedback and Presentation Lifecycle Policy v1

facts.subject: visual/audio feedback authority
facts.statement: Titles, actionbars, particles, sounds, music, animations, render-state indicators, and lobby visual markers are presentation mirrors, not gameplay authority. Gameplay logic must not infer authoritative arena state solely from whether feedback is visible or playing.

facts.subject: feedback ownership
facts.statement: Gameplay-relevant feedback should be owned by player/session or arena generation plus feedbackGeneration and purpose, so stale callbacks cannot overwrite newer titles, music, particles, animations, or status indicators.

facts.subject: arena status indicator
facts.statement: Lobby indicators such as empty/connecting/occupied colors must be derived from authoritative arena state and updated through a single renderer/mirror path. Visual blocks/entities must not independently decide the arena state.

facts.subject: feedback reconciliation
facts.statement: When authoritative state changes, feedback should converge through an idempotent renderer that can repair missing or stale presentation without mutating the underlying gameplay authority.

facts.subject: animation controller transitions
facts.statement: Animation-controller conditions and Molang queries used for gameplay-significant visual states must map to current authoritative or intentionally mirrored entity properties. A visual controller should not encode an independent second state machine that can diverge from gameplay.

facts.subject: looping audio/animation feedback
facts.statement: Looping or long-lived feedback requires an explicit stop/reset contract for arena end, player disconnect, cinematic abort, respawn, and generation replacement. Start-without-stop is a lifecycle defect.

facts.subject: title/actionbar ownership
facts.statement: If multiple systems can write title/actionbar feedback, use purpose/priority arbitration or dedicated channels where possible; unrelated systems must not silently overwrite critical gameplay messages.

facts.subject: feedback audience
facts.statement: Arena-specific feedback must target the current participant/audience set explicitly. Broad @a sound/title/particle/camera-adjacent feedback is prohibited unless intentionally global.

facts.subject: feedback verification
facts.statement: For gameplay-critical presentation such as lobby occupancy markers, ready indicators, objective markers, or cinematic cues, define observable postconditions and repair paths so server-state success is not assumed to imply presentation success.

facts.subject: world-based visual indicators
facts.statement: If status indicators are implemented using blocks/entities restored by structures, world mutation/reset must rebuild and re-render their current authoritative state afterward rather than assuming restored visuals are already correct.

facts.subject: late join/reload visual reconstruction
facts.statement: Feedback systems should support reconstruction when a client joins, reloads, or newly observes an entity. Long-lived visual state must be derivable from current authority/mirrors rather than depending only on a one-time historical event.

facts.subject: animation compatibility
facts.statement: Animation/Molang/controller behavior that depends on format/platform semantics must be linked to the compatibility runtime profile and revalidated after Minecraft updates before visual regressions are blamed solely on gameplay logic.
